notes: Mahwah's initial DCA obligation was 629 units (second highest in Bergen County). Township contested, proposing 444; Program-mediated settlement agreed to 495 on March 31, 2025; Superior Court Order entered April 14, 2025. Fourth Round Present Need Obligation: 224 (per one search synthesis – treat as low-confidence; not traced to primary document). Prospective Need settled at 650 per same synthesis (conflict: Township website says 444 adopted Jan 29, and mediation produced 495 total). The 108-page HEFSP was unanimously adopted by Planning Board and Council on June 23, 2025. The plan invokes the Highlands Water Protection and Planning Act buildout analysis to reduce actual new construction from 495 to only 3 units; remaining 492 units addressed via credits. Plan submitted to Program and court for certification. DCA initial figure was 629; the municipality is in the Highlands Preservation Area which materially limits buildable land.

notes: DCA assigned Midland Park an obligation of 155 affordable units for Round 4. Under the 25% minimum RDP rule, planning for at least 39 units is required (25% of 155). The vacant land assessment found RDP = 0 (no new vacant land identified since prior round). Borough reached a settlement with FSHC in January 2026. HEFSP adopted June 16, 2025 and filed with NJ Courts library. Settlement affirmed RDP of 0. Plan addresses the 39-unit minimum through: (a) proposed new MFO-3 overlay zone (at least 17 affordable units); (b) increased density in existing MFO-2 overlay (at least 10 additional affordable units). Additionally, Block 45 Lot 9.01 (90 Midland Avenue) was rezoned from R-2 to MARD (90 Midland Avenue Redevelopment District), contributing at least 5 affordable units. MFO-1 is approximately 0.85 acres and MFO-2 is approximately 2.15 acres. No active development applications pending as of HEFSP adoption date.
